reason: The cited evidence (E2) discusses oxygen effects on mechanical properties in Nb, not electrical conductivity in HfNbTaTiZr, and E1/E3 are about oxidation and phase stability in Nb-silicide alloys, providing no support for the key premises on electron scattering, conduction pathways, or model accuracy.
premises: Oxygen contamination in HfNbTaTiZr acts as defect sites that alter electron scattering and conduction pathways.
Temperature-dependent electron-phonon interactions are key to conductivity in this alloy.
Existing analytical models assume defect-free crystals and thus over-idealize conduction pathways.
Incorporating defect scattering and temperature effects into a predictive model will significantly improve accuracy over analytical models.
The approach is applicable to bulk HfNbTaTiZr with ~1 wt.% oxygen and similar defect profiles.
